title: Of Sincere Trust in Divine Providence
summary: On the sixth day, the Sixth Wazir addressed King Azadbakht on the role of human effort and divine destiny. Bakhtiyar stood before the throne, his countenance shining with spirit...
full_text:
On the sixth day, the Sixth Wazir addressed King Azadbakht on the role of human effort and divine destiny. Bakhtiyar stood before the throne, his countenance shining with spiritual serenity:

'O King! Human intellect and honest endeavor are necessary duties; we must till the soil, build the ship, and steer with the oar. But he who relies entirely upon his own frail cunning, imagining that his intellect alone commands the universe, is like an ant that thinks it moves the mountain!

True trust in providence is not passive sloth; it is the courage to do what is right, just, and honorable, and then leave the outcome peacefully in the hands of the Creator of all things.

When the storm is fierce and all earthly instruments fail, the soul that trusts in providence remains serene, knowing that behind the darkest cloud shines the sun of divine wisdom.

This unshakeable trust removes fear from the heart, delivers a man from the temptation to compromise his honor for temporary gain, and opens doors of deliverance where human eyes see only sheer stone walls, as the chronicle of King Bakhtzaman illustrates.'
moral: Trust in divine guidance provides peace of soul and delivers the righteous in the hour of trial.
